title: Is multithreading faster on one core?
context: Is running several threads on one core always more efficient?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (1 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: No. On one core, threads share the same CPU time. Each switch has a cost: saving registers, cache pollution and scheduler overhead. CPU-bound work gets no faster and often gets slower. Multithreading helps when threads wait on I/O or sleep, because another thread can run during the wait. Pick the thread count based on whether the work is CPU-bound or I/O-bound.

points.title: Context switch cost
points.why: Switching threads costs CPU time and cache, which slows pure computation.

points.title: I/O-bound work
points.why: Threads that wait on I/O free the core for others, so concurrency helps.
